$comment: The landing lemniscate: which concepts sit on the thread, and where (#52).
ADR-0003 asks for a committed layout rather than a force simulation, so the figure is
byte-identical across builds and a node's position is a decision someone made rather than an
accident of a solver. Before this file, the landing page picked `allNodes.filter(tier)
.slice(0, 3)` — alphabetically first — while a comment above it claimed the layout was
already committed. The right lobe read Adam / AdamW / ALiBi.
POSITION IS `t`, NOT x/y. Each node names a fraction along its lobe, and the renderer
resolves it through `pointAt` in src/lib/curve.ts — the same function that draws the stroke.
Raw coordinates would let a bead drift off the path the moment the curve was nudged; a `t`
cannot. The decision stays committed, the geometry stays derived.
HOW A NODE EARNS A PLACE. The left lobe is gold and holds verified concepts; the right is
teal and holds frontier ones. That is the figure's whole argument — reviewed core flowing
into new growth — so tier decides the lobe and nothing else may.
Within a lobe the bar is RECOGNITION, not centrality. This page has ten seconds to get a
stranger onto a node, so a name someone arriving cold already half-knows is worth more than
the node with the most edges. `causal-masking` outranks `attention` on connectivity and
would be a worse invitation.
Three beads per lobe when there are three to place. The handoff staggers the frontier pulse
over three delays, and labels go on the beads at t=0.2 and t=0.8 and never the one at t=0.5:
mid-lobe is the figure's widest point, and the stroke runs straight through the text there.
That is four labels, which is what the handoff asks for and as many as a 620px figure holds.
Every id here is checked against /content/nodes by `validate:content`, which also rejects a
bead whose tier belongs to the other lobe, a t outside 0-1, and a duplicate.
Written when the left lobe was every verified concept there is. It no longer is — every
concept in the corpus is verified as of #346 — so the left lobe is a CHOICE among many
rather than a listing, and recognition is the whole of the bar. A bead also cannot simply
stay: verifying a node moves it off the teal lobe by force, because validate:content rejects
a bead whose tier belongs to the other one. That is how backpropagation left this file, and
it is what has now emptied the right lobe entirely. When a concept arrives that a stranger
would recognise faster than one of the three on the left, this file is where someone decides
whether it displaces one.
THE RIGHT LOBE IS EMPTY, AND THAT IS A STATE RATHER THAN A GAP (ADR-0015, #283). There is
nothing on the frontier to place, so the figure draws the lobe bare and the landing page
says every concept is reviewed. The next seeded node lands here. Padding it with a verified
concept in the meantime would be the one thing this file exists to prevent — the figure
lying about the tier it encodes.
